doc.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Jeannette: an integrated duplex and being the youngest of nine
summary: Hampton remembers sharing a house with a white family in Jeannette and thinking America was integrated; he was the last of nine children.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let’s start in Jeannette, Pennsylvania. Can you give us a little information about the town and what you recollect of being born there, and your early years?

I didn’t live there very long, but I do remember very strongly that in Jeannette, for some reason I got the impression that all of America was integrated, because we lived in a family – we shared a house with a white family and our family. I thought that it was that way everywhere until we left Jeannette. Then immediately it changed.
So you were living in a duplex, two-family home?
Yes, two-family home. We left there when I was three years old. So we didn’t stay very long, but I had a very good impression of that city.
Where do you fall in the line of Hampton children in your particular family?
There were four sisters and five brothers. I always say that by the time my father got to me, all the perfect pitch and everything was gone.
